key_insight: Piper makes large-scale distributed training more flexible by letting users program how parallelism and execution are composed, instead of hand-coding a fixed strategy for each model. This helps training systems adapt to new combinations of data, pipeline, expert, and memory-saving techniques.
problem_solved: Modern foundation model training is hard to configure because high-level parallelism choices and low-level execution details are often designed manually by experts. Existing frameworks make it difficult to quickly adapt to new training strategies or mix multiple parallelism methods cleanly.
method: Provides a programmable system for expressing distributed training strategies at a higher level.
Connects high-level parallelism plans to low-level execution so multiple strategies can be composed more easily.
Supports combinations of data parallelism, pipeline parallelism, expert parallelism, and optimizations like ZeRO.
impact: For ML practitioners, Piper can reduce the engineering burden of building and modifying large-model training setups. It makes it easier to experiment with new distributed strategies and scale models without redesigning the entire system.

paper_title: Piper: A Programmable Distributed Training System
paper_authors: Megan Frisella, Shubham Tiwari, Andy Ruan, Yi Pan, Parker Gustafson
